content.prompt:
The sum of the ages of two children is 24 and the difference between their ages is 8.
If Nikki is the older sister of Travis, determine their ages by setting up and solving a pair of simultaneous equations.

answer.short: $n$: Nikki’s age in years; $t$: Travis’s age in years.
answer.worked: Let $n$ be Nikki’s age in years and $t$ be Travis’s age in years.
The sum gives $n+t=24$ (1). Nikki is older, so the difference gives $n-t=8$ (2).

Add (1) and (2):
$$\begin{aligned}2n&=32\\n&=16\end{aligned}$$
Substitute $n=16$ into (1):
$$\begin{aligned}16+t&=24\\t&=8\end{aligned}$$

inlines.answer: Nikki is 16 years old and Travis is 8 years old.

answer.short: Nikki is 16 years old and Travis is 8 years old.
answer.worked: Nikki is 16 years old and Travis is 8 years old.

content.prompt: The perimeter of a rectangle is 56 cm. If the length of the rectangle is three times its breadth, determine the dimensions by setting up and solving two simultaneous equations.

answer.short: Let $l$ be the length and $b$ be the breadth, both in centimetres.
answer.worked: Let $l$ be the length and $b$ be the breadth, both in centimetres.
$$\begin{align*}2l+2b&=56\qquad (1)\\l&=3b\qquad (2)\end{align*}$$

Substitute (2) into (1).
$$\begin{align*}2(3b)+2b&=56\\8b&=56\\b&=7\end{align*}$$
Substitute $b=7$ into (2).
$$\begin{align*}l&=3(7)\\l&=21\end{align*}$$
The rectangle is 21 cm long and 7 cm wide.

content.prompt: Adult concert tickets cost $\$5$ more than child tickets. Two adult tickets and two child tickets cost $\$70$ in total. Find the cost of each ticket.

answer.short: Let $a$ be the adult ticket cost and $c$ be the child ticket cost, both in dollars.
answer.worked: Let $a$ be the adult ticket cost and $c$ be the child ticket cost, both in dollars.
$$\begin{align*}a-c&=5\qquad (1)\\2a+2c&=70\qquad (2)\end{align*}$$

Multiply (1) by 2.
$$\begin{align*}2a-2c&=10\qquad (3)\end{align*}$$
Add (2) and (3).
$$\begin{align*}4a&=80\\a&=20\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=20$ into (1).
$$\begin{align*}20-c&=5\\c&=15\end{align*}$$
Each child ticket costs $\$15$ and each adult ticket costs $\$20$.

children.prompt:
John buys three daffodils and five petunias from the nursery and pays $\$25$.

Julia buys four daffodils and three petunias for $\$26$.

Determine the cost of each type of flower.

answer.worked:
Let $d$ be the cost of one daffodil in dollars and $p$ the cost of one petunia in dollars.

$$\begin{align*}3d+5p&=25 &&\text{(1)}\\4d+3p&=26 &&\text{(2)}\\9d+15p&=75 &&3\times\text{(1)}\\20d+15p&=130 &&5\times\text{(2)}\\11d&=55 &&5\times\text{(2)}-3\times\text{(1)}\\d&=5\end{align*}$$

Substitute $d=5$ into (1):

$$\begin{align*}3(5)+5p&=25\\5p&=10\\p&=2\end{align*}$$

Each daffodil costs $\$5$ and each petunia costs $\$2$.

children.prompt: Alex buys 4 bolts and 6 washers for $\$2.20$ and Holly spends $\$1.80$ on 3 bolts and 5 washers at the same local hardware store. Determine the costs of each bolt and each washer.

answer.worked:
Let $b$ be the cost of one bolt in dollars and $w$ the cost of one washer in dollars.

$$\begin{align*}4b+6w&=2.20 &&\text{(1)}\\3b+5w&=1.80 &&\text{(2)}\\12b+18w&=6.60 &&3\times\text{(1)}\\12b+20w&=7.20 &&4\times\text{(2)}\\2w&=0.60 &&4\times\text{(2)}-3\times\text{(1)}\\w&=0.30\end{align*}$$

Substitute $w=0.30$ into (2):

$$\begin{align*}3b+5(0.30)&=1.80\\3b&=0.30\\b&=0.10\end{align*}$$

Each bolt costs $\$0.10$ and each washer costs $\$0.30$.

inlines.text: A scientist mixes a 10% saline solution with a 30% saline solution to produce 200 mL of a 25% saline solution. Find the volume of each solution used.

inlines.latex: \begin{aligned}x&=\text{volume of 10\% solution in mL},\\y&=\text{volume of 30\% solution in mL}.\end{aligned}

answer.short: 50 mL of the 10% solution and 150 mL of the 30% solution.
answer.worked:
Using the variables in the hint, the total volume and the amount of salt give:

$$\begin{align*}x+y&=200 &&\text{(1)}\\0.10x+0.30y&=0.25(200) &&\text{(2)}\\x+3y&=500 &&10\times\text{(2)}\\2y&=300 &&10\times\text{(2)}-\text{(1)}\\y&=150\end{align*}$$

Substitute $y=150$ into (1):

$$\begin{align*}x+150&=200\\x&=50\end{align*}$$

Use 50 mL of the 10% solution and 150 mL of the 30% solution.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
A rectangle has area of $40\text{ m}^2$. Its length is $3\text{ m}$ longer than its breadth.
Find the length of the rectangle.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the breadth in metres.
$$\begin{align*}x(x+3)&=40\\x^2+3x-40&=0\\(x+8)(x-5)&=0\\x&=-8\text{ or }5\end{align*}$$
Since $x>0$, the breadth is $5\text{ m}$.
The length is $5+3=8\text{ m}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
A triangle has area of $24\text{ m}^2$. Its height is $2\text{ m}$ more than its base.
Calculate the length of the base.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the base length in metres. The height is $(x+2)\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac12x(x+2)&=24\\x(x+2)&=48\\x^2+2x-48&=0\\(x+8)(x-6)&=0\\x&=-8\text{ or }6\end{align*}$$
Since $x>0$, the base is $6\text{ m}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt:
A rectangular garden, $10\text{ m}$ by $6\text{ m}$, is surrounded by a paved path of uniform width.
If the area of the path alone is $80\text{ m}^2$, find its width.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the path width in metres. The outer dimensions are $(10+2x)\text{ m}$ and $(6+2x)\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}(10+2x)(6+2x)-60&=80\\60+32x+4x^2-60&=80\\4x^2+32x-80&=0\\x^2+8x-20&=0\\(x+10)(x-2)&=0\\x&=-10\text{ or }2\end{align*}$$
Since $x>0$, the path is $2\text{ m}$ wide.
Check: $14\times10-10\times6=80\text{ m}^2$.

entries.description:
Apply Simultaneous Equations to Solve Problems
When a scenario has two variables that aren’t directly related to each other, we need to set up two equations and solve them simultaneously.

entries.description:
Example Apply simultaneous equations to solve problems
The sum of the ages of two children is 17 and the difference in their ages is 5.
If Karla is the older sister of Alice, determine their ages.
entries.presentation: Light peach activity heading; prompt above two columns of working.

entries.description:
1. Let k be Karla’s age. Let a be Alice’s age.
2. k + a = 17  (1)
   k − a = 5  (2)
3. (1) + (2): 2k = 22
               k = 11
3. (cont.) Sub k = 11 into (1)
           11 + b = 17
                b = 6
4. Karla is 11 and Alice is 6
